name: SikaGrout-300 PT AU
paste:
SIKAGROUT®-300 PT AU: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: SikaGrout®-300 PT AU, December 2020, Version 01.02 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/9/sikagrout_-300_ptau.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide SikaGrout®-300 PT AU where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (December 2020, Version 01.02).
1.2 Product description. SikaGrout®-300 PT AU is a non-shrink (Class A and C), cementitious grout with a unique 2 phase shrinkage compensating mechanism. It is non-metallic and contains no chlorides. With a special blend of shrinkage reducing and plasticizing/water- reducing agents, SikaGrout®-300 PT AU compensates for shrinkage in both the plastic and hardened states.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer. SikaGrout®-300 PT AU suitably experienced and trained specialist contractors. SikaGrout®-300 PT AU is used:
    - For horizontal and vertical grouting of ducts within bonded, post-tensioned structures
    - To grout and fill or repair voids within ducts of posttensioning strands for corrosion protection
    - For grouting with tight clearance requirements
1.4 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.7.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. SikaGrout®-300 PT AU
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: High Performance, Zero Bleed, Sand Free, Cementitious Grout for Post-Tensioning Applications
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Approvals / certificates.
    - RMS B113- Post Tensioning of Concrete
    - RMS R56 Ground Anchors
    - RMS R64 Soil Nailing
    - Dept Transport Qld (TMR )- Product Index for bridges and other Structures Section 5. Registered and Conforming Products Part 5.30 Post Tensioning Grout
2.3 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - ASTM C 1152: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Product Information > Soluble chloride ion content (p.2).
    - ASTM C 1090: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Shrinkage (p.2).
    - ASTM C 940: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Bleeding (p.2); Technical Information > Expansion (p.2).
    - ASTM C 939: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Application Information > Flowability (p.2).
2.4 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Sand free allows filling and repairing of voids with-inducts of post-tensioned structures
    - Does not contain aluminium powder or any components which generate hydrogen gas, carbon dioxide or oxygen Silica fume enhanced for low permeability
    - For additional protection, substitute 74 ml of mixing water with 74 ml of Sika® Ferrogard® -901 for each 20 kg bag of SikaGrout® -300 PT AU
    - Easy to use, just add water
    - Non metallic, will not stain or rust
    - Zero bleeding, even at high flow
    - Low heat build-up
    - Excellent for pumping. Does not segregate even at high flow and no build-up on equipment or hoppers
    - Non-corrosive, does not contain chlorides
    - Superior freeze/ thaw resistance
2.5 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Composition: Portland cement
    - Density: ~ 2.0 kg/litre
2.6 Properties stated by the manufacturer.
    - Maximum grain size: None (sand free)
    - Soluble chloride ion content: < 0.08% by weight of cementitious material (ASTM C 1152)
    - Expansion: < 2% after 3 hours (ASTM C 940)
    - Bleeding: <0.5% (ASTM C 940)
2.7 Compressive strength.
    | Day | W/P: 0.33 @ 23oC |
    | 1 | ~ 15 MPa |
    | 7 | ~ 55 MPa |
    | 28 | ~ 65 MPa |
    Test method printed: (RMS T375)
2.8 Shrinkage.
    | Day | W/P: 0.33 @ 23oC |
    | 1 | 0 - 0.1% |
    | 28 | 0 - 0.2% |
    Test method printed: (ASTM C 1090)
2.9 Electrical resistivity.
    | 7 days | ~ 4,000 Ω.cm |
    | 28 days | ~ 10,000 Ω.cm |
    | 56 days | ~ 13,000 Ω.cm |
    | 90 days | ~ 14,000 Ω.cm |
    Test method printed: (FM5-578)
    Note printed: 50mm Probe Spacing
2.10 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Packaging: 20 kg bags
    - Shelf life: 9 months from date of production
    - Storage conditions: Store properly in dry conditions in undamaged and unopened original sealed packaging

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (December 2020, Version 01.02) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate quality / pre-treatment.
    - Cable Duct grouting
    - Ensure that ducts, openings, voids, inlets and outlets are clean and free of debris, fuel, oils, other contaminants and site debris at all times.
    - Other grouting applications
    - Remove all dirt, oil, grease, and other bond-inhibiting materials by mechanical means. Anchor bolts to be grouted must be de-greased with suitable solvent which will not inhibit grout bonding. Concrete must be sound and roughened to promote mechanical adhesion. Prior to placing, surface should be brought to a saturated surface dry (SDD) condition. Ensure forms and ducts will retain grout without leakage.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (December 2020, Version 01.02) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Mixing ratio: 6.6 litres of water per 20kg bag for RMS B113, R56 & R64 compliant grout
    - Yield: 1 bag yields approx. 12.4 - 13.6litre of grout depending on water addition
    - Pot Life: ~ 60 minutes
4.3 Flowability.
    | W/P ratio | Initial Flow (sec) | Flow Retention @ |
    | 45 mins (sec) |
    | 0.33 | < 20 | < 3 change |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
    Test method printed: (ASTM C 939)
4.4 Mixing.
    - For best resutls use a colloidal mixer. Alternatively, mechanically mix with a high speed drill (2500 rpm) and Sika® jiffy paddle. Mix for approximately 3 minutes after the addition of the last bag or until a homogeneus mix is achieved. Continue to agitate material in the holding hopper to achieve optimum flow. The method of mixing may significantly affect the material properties, particularly flow. At higher temperatures and/or with higher water amounts, the grout will behave less thixotropically. Therefore, it may be more appropiate to measure the flow using the standard flow cone test (ASTM C -939). The expected flux time is between 11 - 20 seconds under normal conditions. Specific on site testing by the engineer is recommended to ensure that the mixing and placement methods result in the specified requirements.
    - Add appropiate quantity of clean water. Add bag of material to mixing vessel. Start by using 5.4 litres of water per 20 kg bag of material. Add additional water as needed - a total maximum of 6.6 litres per 20 kg bag in order to achieve the flow specified. Ambient and material temperature should be as close as possible to +23 °C. If higher, use cold water, if colder, use warm water.
4.5 Application.
    - Make sure all forming, mixing, placing, and clean-up materials are on hand. The grout should be used within 60 minutes from the start of mixing. The method of pumping the grout must ensure complete filling of the ducts and complete surrounding of the strands or bar. A mock-up should be completed on onsite and inspected by the engineer to ensure that the placement means and methods yield the specified results.
    - When grouting ducts or other critical elements, it is higly recommended that experienced, trained technicians complete the work.
4.6 Cleaning of equipment. Clean all the tools and application equipment with water immediately after use. Hardened/ cured material can only be mechanically removed.
4.7 Limitations and important considerations.
    - Minimum application thickness: 3 mm
    - Maximum application thickness (neat): comply with PTI (Post- tensioning Institute) specification for grouting of post-tensioned structures
    - Do not use as a patching or overlay mortar or in unconfined areas
    - Material must be placed within 60 minutes of mixing
    - As with all cement based materials, avoid contact with aluminium to prevent adverse chemical reaction and possible product failure. Insulate potential areas of contact by coating aluminium bars, rails, post, etc. with an appropiate epoxy coating.
    - Minimum ambient and substrate temperature +5 °C and rising at time of application. For lower temperature, refer to the Post-Tensioning Institute (PTI) Guide Specification for Grouting of Post- Tensioned Structures.
    - Maximum ambient and substrate temperature is 35°C at the time of placement. For higher temperatures, refer to the PTI Guide Specification for Grouting of Post-Tensioned Structures.

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Ambient air temperature. +5 °C min / +35 °C max
5.3 Substrate temperature. +5 °C min / +35 °C max
5.4 Conditions stated in the limitations. Also stated in the data sheet limitations (clause 4.7):
    - Minimum ambient and substrate temperature +5 °C and rising at time of application. For lower temperature, refer to the Post-Tensioning Institute (PTI) Guide Specification for Grouting of Post- Tensioned Structures.
    - Maximum ambient and substrate temperature is 35°C at the time of placement. For higher temperatures, refer to the PTI Guide Specification for Grouting of Post-Tensioned Structures.
5.5 Trials, test areas and compatibility checks stated by the manufacturer.
    - Make sure all forming, mixing, placing, and clean-up materials are on hand. The grout should be used within 60 minutes from the start of mixing. The method of pumping the grout must ensure complete filling of the ducts and complete surrounding of the strands or bar. A mock-up should be completed on onsite and inspected by the engineer to ensure that the placement means and methods yield the specified results.
5.6 Test methods printed beside stated values. Each value is as printed in the data sheet with its test method.
    - Soluble chloride ion content: < 0.08% by weight of cementitious material (ASTM C 1152)
    - Compressive strength: Day | W/P: 0.33 @ 23oC; 1 | ~ 15 MPa; 7 | ~ 55 MPa; 28 | ~ 65 MPa (RMS T375)
    - Shrinkage: Day | W/P: 0.33 @ 23oC; 1 | 0 - 0.1%; 28 | 0 - 0.2% (ASTM C 1090)
    - Expansion: < 2% after 3 hours (ASTM C 940)
    - Bleeding: <0.5% (ASTM C 940)
    - Electrical resistivity: 7 days | ~ 4,000 Ω.cm; 28 days | ~ 10,000 Ω.cm; 56 days | ~ 13,000 Ω.cm; 90 days | ~ 14,000 Ω.cm (FM5-578)
    - Flowability: W/P ratio | Initial Flow (sec) | Flow Retention @; 45 mins (sec); 0.33 | < 20 | < 3 change (ASTM C 939)
5.7 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.8 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: SikaGrout®-300 PT AU, December 2020, Version 01.02, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/9/sikagrout_-300_ptau.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SikaGrout 300 PT AU, version 05/05/2025, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/m/MSDS%20SikaGrout%20-%20300%20PT%20AU%20GHS7.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS SikaGrout®-300 PT AU, version 20/11/2025, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/2/sds-sikagrout-300ptau.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
